Figures describe the Méribel valley (the resort's own pass). Search summary of meribel.net and OnTheSnow: 150 km of slopes, 72 runs, 43 lifts (gondolas, high-speed chairlifts and surface lifts — counts by type not found). Terrain split as published by OnTheSnow: 11% beginner, 38% intermediate, 39% advanced, 13% expert (sums to 101% from rounding). Linked Les 3 Vallées area (official 'in figures' page, search summary): 600 km of pistes, 334 pistes (53 green, 136 blue, 108 red, 37 black), 161 lifts, of which the summary itemised 34 gondolas, 3 cable cars, 57 chairlifts and 33 drag lifts (the other 34 not broken down); Wikipedia puts total uplift at about 284,500 skiers/hour in 2026 (estimate). Re-checked 2026-10-03: search summaries again give 150 km for the Méribel valley; lift count 43 vs 46 depending on source. 2026-10-03 CI-fetched official pages: meribel.net 'Domaine Méribel — 150 km de pistes' and 3 Vallées 600 km; the S3V price page says 'more than 70 high-altitude runs'. character: Méribel lies in the central valley of Les 3 Vallées, with its main villages at Méribel (about 1,450 m) and Méribel-Mottaret (about 1,750 m) and a gondola up from Brides-les-Bains. The Méribel valley has about 150 km of pistes and 43 lifts, and links over the ridges to Courchevel and to Val Thorens and Les Menuires within the 600 km 3 Vallées area.
learning: About 11% of the terrain is rated beginner (OnTheSnow split, search summary). Reference: there are beginner areas at Méribel (Altiport) and Mottaret; confirm beginner-lift access and lessons for 2026-27.
